supplier_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ bound a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$. Choose a disk-band decomposition of $F$ with one disk and $2g$ bands, and use its band-core basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ to form the positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For $q\ge2$, define the symmetric block matrix $M_q(V)$ of size $2g(q-1)$ by specifying its $2g\times2g$ blocks, indexed by $1\le k,\ell\le q-1$:
$$(M_q(V))_{k\ell}=\begin{cases}V+V^T,&k=\ell,\\-V^T,&\ell=k+1,\\-V,&k=\ell+1,\\0,&|k-\ell|\ge2.\end{cases}$$
Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, cut $B^4$ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface, and take $q$ copies. For $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue the positive face of copy $i$ to the negative face of copy $i+1$ by reflecting the normal coordinate; do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face. Call the resulting $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $W_q(F)$. It has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.

supplier_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $J=J_1\cup\cdots\cup J_n$ be an oriented link of $n\ge1$ smooth components in $S^3$. Choose pairwise disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(J_i)$, let $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_iN(J_i))$, and let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian of $J_i$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the longitude parallel to $J_i$ with zero self-linking. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^n$ on the meridian basis $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_n]$; for $i\ne j$, define $\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ to be the $j$-th coordinate of $[\lambda_i]$, the usual oriented linking number. Use the boundary-torus intersection convention $\mu_i\mathbin{\cdot}\lambda_i=+1$. Give $J_i$ an integer framing $f_i$ and fill along $\delta_i=\lambda_i+f_i\mu_i$. Let $A$ be the symmetric integer matrix with $A_{ii}=f_i$ and $A_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ for $i\ne j$. Assume $\det A\ne0$, and let $Y$ be the resulting oriented surgery manifold, oriented as the boundary of the 4-dimensional surgery handlebody with outward normal first. Then $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^n/A\mathbb Z^n$. For torsion classes $[C],[D]\in H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ represented by oriented 1-cycles, choose $m>0$ and an integral 2-chain $F$ with $\partial F=mC$ and define $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\mathbin{\cdot}D)/m\pmod{\mathbb Z}$, where the intersection is signed by the orientation of $Y$. If $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ are meridian-coordinate representatives of $[C],[D]$, then
$$
\lambda_Y([x],[y])=-x^TA^{-1}y\pmod{\mathbb Z}.
$$

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose core has self-linking $+1$ in the positive-push convention. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\chi:H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ have prime-power order $d$. Choose a Casson–Gordon bordism datum $(M_{0,q},\eta,r,W)$. Write $G=\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$, let $Y\to W$ be the regular cover determined by $\eta$, and give $\mathbb C(t)$ the $G$-action $(a,n)z=\exp(2\pi ia/d)t^n z$ and involution $\overline{t}=t^{-1}$ with complex conjugation on constants. Define
$$H_2^t(W;\mathbb C)=H_2(Y;\mathbb C)\otimes_{\mathbb C[G]}\mathbb C(t).$$
The Casson–Gordon Witt class is
$$\tau(\Sigma_q(K),\chi)=\frac{1}{r}\bigl([H_2^t(W;\mathbb C)]-[H_2(W;\mathbb C)\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(t)]\bigr)\in W(\mathbb C(t))\otimes\mathbb Q,$$
using the capped nonsingular twisted and untwisted Hermitian forms. Here $W(\mathbb C(t))$ is the Witt group of nonsingular Hermitian forms over the field with involution, modulo hyperbolic forms. Its signature defect is $\sigma(K,\chi)=\sigma_1(\tau(\Sigma_q(K),\chi))$, where $\sigma_1$ evaluates a Hermitian representative at $t=e^{i\theta}$ and takes the one-sided limit as $\theta\to0^+$. This is the specified Casson–Gordon invariant and signature homomorphism; it is not an arbitrary rho invariant or an unspecified difference of signatures.

supplier_excerpt: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, choose its compact exterior $E_K$ with boundary torus $T_K$, and let $\mu$ and $\lambda$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude. The exterior homology theorem gives $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z$ be the composite of abelianization with the homomorphism $[\mu]\mapsto1$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $\phi_q$ be the composite $\pi_1(E_K)\xrightarrow{\phi}\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, and let $p_q:E_q\to E_K$ be the connected cover classified by $\ker\phi_q$. On $T_K$, the homomorphism sends $[\mu]\mapsto1$ and $[\lambda]\mapsto0$, so the preimage of $T_K$ is a connected torus cover whose fundamental group corresponds to $\langle\mu^q,\lambda\rangle$. Let $\widetilde\mu$ be the closed lift of $\mu^q$. Attach a solid torus to $E_q$ with its meridian identified with $\widetilde\mu$; the resulting oriented closed $3$-manifold is the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $\Sigma_q(K)$. In tubular coordinates near $K$, the extended map to $S^3$ has local form $(s,w)\mapsto(s,w^q)$, and the deck group $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$ acts by $w\mapsto e^{2\pi i/q}w$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
